mainTopic: Right-hand scooping for רבי שמעון, and the rules for collecting the blood straight from the animal into the vessel
overview: The amud opens with a question on רבי שמעון. Why would he need רבא's גזירה שוה from the word "יד" (hand) to require the right hand? The scooping (קמיצה) already needs the right hand, from "כחטאת וכאשם" as רב יהודה בריה דרבי חייא explains it. The answer is that the גזירה שוה is needed for the מנחת חוטא. That offering is kept plain on purpose, so we might have thought a left-hand scooping is fine. Next, a new משנה rules that blood which spilled on the floor and was then gathered up is פסול. A ברייתא learns this from "מִדַּם הַפָּר", read as "דָּם מֵהַפָּר": the blood must go straight from the bull into the vessel. The ברייתא gets this reading through גורעין ומוסיפין ודורשין. The גמרא then defends רב's rule that all the bull's blood must be collected, using אם אינו ענין. It also brings שמואל's rule that the שוחט must hold the knife up, and אביי's answer that the knife is wiped on the rim of the bowl. The amud ends as רב חסדא begins another rule about the שוחט, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why does רבי שמעון need רבא's "hand"–"hand" teaching?
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי שמעון, the קומץ either needs no holy vessel or may go into one with the left hand. So what is רבא's גזירה שוה of "יד"–"יד" there to teach?
steps.simpleTranslation: There are two ways to understand רבי שמעון. One says he does not require putting the handful into a holy vessel. The other says he does require it, but allows it with the left hand. Either way, why would he need רבא's teaching from the word "hand" appearing in two places?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי שמעון would need רבא's "יד"–"יד" גזירה שוה at all. For him, the vessel step either does not exist or may be done with the left hand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's גזירה שוה teaches that something must be done with the right hand. But for רבי שמעון, the step of putting the קומץ in a vessel (קידוש קומץ) either is not needed or is fine with the left hand. So the גמרא wants to know which job the גזירה שוה is still doing for him.

keyTerms.meaning: Making the handful holy by placing it in a holy service vessel
The handful of flour scooped from a meal offering and burned on the altar
Left hand
He deems it fit (valid)
Why do I need it? (a sign that something looks unnecessary)

phrases.aramaic: וּלְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן – דְּלָא בָּעֵי קִידּוּשׁ קוֹמֶץ;
phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Shimon, who does not require sanctifying the handful;

phrases.aramaic: וּלְמַאן דְּאָמַר לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן נָמֵי בָּעֵי קִידּוּשׁ –
phrases.english: and according to the one who says that Rabbi Shimon also requires sanctification,
he deems the handful [placed in a vessel] with the left hand to be fit;
why do I need Rava's "hand"–"hand" teaching?
phrases.notes: This points back to רבא's earlier גזירה שוה, which links two פסוקים that both use the word "hand."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question about how רבא's earlier גזירה שוה fits רבי שמעון's view.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for רבא's "יד"–"יד" גזירה שוה according to רבי שמעון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: For רבי שמעון, the vessel step either does not exist or may be done with the left hand, so the right-hand derivation seems to have nothing to teach.

steps.title: It cannot be needed for the scooping itself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא blocks a possible answer: the right-hand rule for the scooping itself is already known from רב יהודה בריה דרבי חייא.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want to say the teaching is needed for the scooping itself, that cannot be. We already learn that from רב יהודה, the son of רבי חייא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shuts down the obvious answer before anyone gives it. It is setting up the quote of רב יהודה בריה דרבי חייא in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might say רבא's גזירה שוה teaches that the scooping (קמיצה) needs the right hand. But that rule already comes from another source, so the גזירה שוה would still be extra. This keeps the question alive.

keyTerms.meaning: The act of scooping the handful from the meal offering
It comes out (is learned) from

phrases.english: If [you say it is needed] for the scooping itself,

phrases.aramaic: מִדְּרַב יְהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא נָפְקָא;
phrases.english: that is already learned from Rav Yehuda, son of Rabbi Chiya;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens the question in step 1 by ruling out the most natural answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: The possible answer that the גזירה שוה teaches the right-hand rule for קמיצה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That rule already has a different source, so the גזירה שוה would be repeating it.

steps.title: רב יהודה's source: "like a sin offering and like a guilt offering"
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה בריה דרבי חייא explains רבי שמעון from the פסוק "כחטאת וכאשם." Done by hand, it must be the right hand, like a חטאת. Done with a vessel, the left hand is fine, like an אשם.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה, son of רבי חייא, said: What is רבי שמעון's reason? The פסוק says, "It is most holy, like the sin offering and like the guilt offering." If the כהן does it by hand, he must use his right hand, like a sin offering. If he does it with a vessel, he may use his left hand, like a guilt offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רב יהודה's teaching to show where the right-hand rule for scooping already comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק compares the מנחה to both a חטאת and an אשם. A חטאת's blood is put on the altar by hand, so anything done by hand must use the right hand. An אשם's blood is put on from a vessel, so a step done with a vessel may use the left hand. Scooping is done by hand, so it needs the right hand, and רבא's גזירה שוה seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: Most holy (the highest level of offerings)
Like the sin offering and like the guilt offering
He performs it (does the service)
Right hand
A vessel (here, a holy service vessel)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two sides. "Like a חטאת" means the right hand is required, because it is done by hand. "Like an אשם" means the left hand is allowed, because it is done with a vessel.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא:
phrases.english: For Rav Yehuda, son of Rabbi Chiya, said:
What is the reason of Rabbi Shimon?
Because the verse says:
"It is most holy, like the sin offering and like the guilt offering";
if he comes to perform it by hand,
he performs it with the right hand, like a sin offering;
if he comes to perform it with a vessel,
he may perform it with the left hand, like a guilt offering!

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the actual source that step 2 referred to.
steps.raayaObject: That the right-hand rule for קמיצה is already known without רבא's גזירה שוה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The פסוק "קדש קדשים היא כחטאת וכאשם" as explained by רב יהודה בריה דרבי חייא

steps.title: Needed for the sinner's meal offering
steps.stepSummary: The גזירה שוה is needed for the מנחת חוטא. Since רבי שמעון says that offering is kept plain on purpose, we might have thought a left-hand scooping is fine there.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed only for scooping the sinner's meal offering. You might have thought this: רבי שמעון said the sinner's offering should not be fancy. So if the כהן scooped it with his left hand, that should also be fine. The גזירה שוה teaches us that it is not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבא's גזירה שוה has a special job. It teaches that even a מנחת חוטא must be scooped with the right hand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון holds that a sinner's offering is kept plain so it will not look fancy. That might suggest that a weaker, left-handed scooping is acceptable for it. The גזירה שוה blocks that idea and requires the right hand even here.

keyTerms.meaning: A sinner's meal offering (brought for certain sins, without oil and frankincense)
You might have thought
Fancy, of the best quality
It teaches us (that this is not so)
It is needed only for

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי שמעון, "כחטאת וכאשם" already teaches that scooping needs the right hand. רבא's "יד"–"יד" is still needed for the מנחת חוטא, so we don't think its "plain" status allows a left-hand scooping.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a teaching which looks extra may be protecting against a mistaken conclusion in one special case.

phrases.english: It is needed only for scooping the meal offering of a sinner;
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is added in the corrected wording.

phrases.english: you might have thought,
since Rabbi Shimon said
that his offering should not be fancy,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי קָמַץ לַהּ בִּשְׂמֹאל נָמֵי תִּיתַּכְשַׁר;
phrases.english: when he scoops it with the left hand, it should also be fit;
so it teaches us [that it is not].

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא נִצְרְכָא אֶלָּא לְקוֹמֵץ מִנְחַת חוֹטֵא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of steps 1–3 by finding a special case the גזירה שוה is needed for.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the teaching to a special case (מנחת חוטא) where a mistaken conclusion was possible
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since a sinner's offering is kept plain, a left-hand scooping might be acceptable for it.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even a מנחת חוטא must be scooped with the right hand, as learned from רבא's "יד"–"יד".

steps.title: Blood that spilled on the floor is disqualified
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that if the blood spilled on the floor and the כהן then gathered it into a vessel, it is פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If the blood spilled onto the floor and the כהן gathered it up, it is disqualified.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts. It rules that blood which hit the floor before it was caught in a כלי שרת cannot be used, even if the כהן collects it afterward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קבלה, catching the blood, has to happen as the blood comes out of the animal. Blood scooped up from the floor was never properly caught, so the עבודה is פסול. The גמרא will now look for the source of this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: spilled
the floor of the עזרה
he gathered it up
disqualified

phrases.english: MISHNA:
If the blood spilled onto the floor,
and he gathered it up – it is disqualified.

steps.triggerLanguage: נִשְׁפַּךְ הַדָּם עַל הָרִצְפָּה, וַאֲסָפוֹ – פָּסוּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה after the discussion of רבי שמעון and the right hand.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blood that spilled on the floor and was then collected is פסול for זריקה.

steps.title: Only the life-blood is valid
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from "מִדַּם הַפָּר" that the כהן must use דם הנפש, not blood from the skin and not דם התמצית.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The Sages taught: "And the anointed כהן shall take from the blood of the bull." This means the life-blood, not blood from the skin and not the blood that trickles out afterward.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא on the פסוק about the פר כהן משיח. Its first lesson is about which blood counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the blood that gushes out at the moment of שחיטה, the blood the animal dies with, is valid. Blood from cutting the skin before the שחיטה is excluded. So is the slow trickle after the main flow stops. This first lesson is a separate rule; the ברייתא's next line is what bears on our משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: the anointed כהן, the כהן גדול
the life-blood that flows out at the שחיטה
the blood that trickles out after the main flow

phrases.english: GEMARA:
The Sages taught:
"And the anointed priest shall take
from the blood of the bull" –
from the blood of the soul,
phrases.notes: He means the blood the animal's life goes out with, the gush at the שחיטה.

phrases.english: and not from the blood of the skin,
and not from the blood of exudate.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: וְלָקַח הַכֹּהֵן הַמָּשִׁיחַ מִדַּם הַפָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the ברייתא that will supply the source for the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only דם הנפש is valid; blood from the skin and דם התמצית are not.

steps.title: Rereading the פסוק as blood from the bull
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא reads "מִדַּם הַפָּר" as if it said "דָּם מֵהַפָּר," that the כהן must collect the blood straight from the bull.
steps.simpleTranslation: "From the blood of the bull" means: he must collect blood from the bull.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a second reading of the same words. This is the source for our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words should be read as "blood from the bull." That means the blood must go straight from the animal into the vessel. Blood that first landed on the floor did not come into the vessel "from the bull," so it is פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: "from the blood of the bull" (the פסוק as written)
"blood from the bull" (the new reading)
he shall collect it

phrases.english: "From the blood of the bull" –
he shall collect blood from the bull.
phrases.notes: The מ at the start of מדם moves over to הפר, so the words read דם מהפר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second lesson from the same words, and the direct source for the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blood must be collected directly from the animal; blood from the floor is פסול.

steps.title: Why the plain reading cannot be right
steps.stepSummary: If "מִדַּם" meant "some of the blood," that would clash with רב, who rules that all the bull's blood must be collected, based on "וְאֵת כׇּל דָּמוֹ יִשְׁפֹּךְ."
steps.simpleTranslation: For if you think "from the blood" means what it seems to say, that even some of the blood is enough, then that clashes with רב. רב said one who slaughters must collect all the bull's blood, because the פסוק says "and all its blood he shall pour out"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves that the plain meaning, "take some of the blood," cannot be what the פסוק means. That is why the ברייתא had to reread it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read simply, "מִדַּם" sounds like "take part of the blood." But רב says every drop of the bull's blood must be collected, because the פסוק says "all its blood" is poured out, and that is only possible if all of it was collected. Since the simple reading clashes with that rule, the מ must be teaching something else.

keyTerms.meaning: if it would enter your mind
as it is written, read simply
a part, some
but didn't (he) say? (introduces a clashing source)

phrases.english: For if it enters your mind
that "from the blood of the bull" means just as it is written –
"from the blood," meaning even some of the blood;
but didn't רב say:
one who slaughters must collect
all the blood of the bull,
as it says: "And all its blood he shall pour out"!

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ מִדַּם הַפָּר כְּדִכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows why the reading in step 7 is needed: the plain reading fails.
steps.raayaObject: That "מִדַּם הַפָּר" cannot mean "some of the blood" and must be reread.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב's ruling that all the bull's blood must be collected, from "וְאֵת כׇּל דָּמוֹ יִשְׁפֹּךְ" (ויקרא 4:7).

steps.title: Conclusion: moving a letter to learn a lesson
steps.stepSummary: So "מִדַּם הַפָּר" means "דָּם מֵהַפָּר," and the ברייתא holds גורעין ומוסיפין ודורשין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, "from the blood of the bull" means: he must collect blood from the bull. And this Sage holds that we may take away a letter, add it elsewhere, and learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the plain reading has been rejected, the גמרא restates the ברייתא's reading. It then names the method the ברייתא's Sage must hold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: גורעין ומוסיפין ודורשין means we may take a letter off one word (the מ of מדם) and add it to the next word (הפר). This gives "דם מהפר," blood straight from the bull. That reading is the source for the משנה: blood from the floor is פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: rather
he holds
we take away a letter, add it elsewhere, and learn from the result

steps.whatToRemember: Blood must go straight from the animal into the vessel. We learn this from "דָּם מֵהַפָּר," read by moving the מ, which is the method of גורעין ומוסיפין ודורשין. That is why blood gathered from the floor is פסול.
steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא is not saying the כהן may collect only part of the blood. רב holds all of it must be collected. The extra מ teaches that the blood must come "from the bull" directly, not that a portion is enough.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the משנה's rule. It also shows a method of reading פסוקים, גורעין ומוסיפין ודורשין, that not every Sage accepts.

phrases.english: Rather, "from the blood of the bull" –
he shall collect blood from the bull.
And he holds:
phrases.notes: "He" is the Sage of this ברייתא.

phrases.english: we subtract, add, and expound.
phrases.notes: The מ is taken off מדם and added to הפר.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מִדַּם הַפָּר – דָּם מֵהַפָּר יְקַבְּלֶנּוּ. וְקָסָבַר: גּוֹרְעִין וּמוֹסִיפִין וְדוֹרְשִׁין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the plain reading is rejected, the ברייתא confirms its reading and names its method.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: "מִדַּם הַפָּר" is read as "דָּם מֵהַפָּר" through גורעין ומוסיפין ודורשין. The blood must be collected straight from the animal, so blood from the floor is פסול.

steps.title: רב: All the bull's blood must be collected
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to רב's statement. The שוחט must collect all the blood of the פר, based on the פסוק ״וְאֵת כׇּל דַּם הַפָּר יִשְׁפֹּךְ״.
steps.simpleTranslation: The matter itself: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: the one who slaughters must collect all the blood of the bull, as it says, "And all the blood of the bull he shall pour out."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now studies, on its own terms, the statement of רב that it used a moment ago. רב says all of the bull's blood must be collected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, in Step 8, רב's rule was only a tool for reading ״מִדַּם הַפָּר״. Now the גמרא examines the rule itself and its source. The proof is the word כׇּל, meaning "all" the blood.

keyTerms.meaning: "The matter itself." The גמרא is returning to look closely at a statement it quoted earlier.
The one who slaughters the animal.
Collecting the blood in a vessel.
Bull. Here it is the bull brought as a חטאת.

phrases.english: The matter itself:
phrases.notes: We're going back to רב's rule, quoted earlier in step 8, to look at it on its own.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
The one who slaughters must collect
all the blood of the bull,
as it is said: "And all the blood of the bull he shall pour out."

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוּפָא – אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to examine רב's rule, which Step 8 used as support.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שוחט must collect all of the bull's blood, learned from ״וְאֵת כׇּל דַּם הַפָּר יִשְׁפֹּךְ״.

steps.title: But that verse is about the leftover blood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the פסוק רב quoted is about the שיריים, the blood left over after sprinkling. It is not about collecting the blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that verse is written about the leftover blood!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב's source. The פסוק talks about pouring out the leftover blood, not about collecting it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In context, ״יִשְׁפֹּךְ״ describes pouring the remaining blood on the base of the מזבח after the sprinklings. So how can רב use it to teach a rule about קבלה at the time of slaughter?

keyTerms.meaning: The leftover blood after the sprinklings. It is poured on the base of the מזבח.
"But isn't it written..." This opens a challenge from the context of a פסוק.

phrases.english: But it is written about the leftover blood!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the source of רב's rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's use of ״וְאֵת כׇּל דַּם הַפָּר יִשְׁפֹּךְ״ as a source for קבלה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In its context the פסוק is about pouring out the שיריים, not about collecting the blood.

steps.title: The verse can't mean the leftovers, so apply it to collecting
steps.stepSummary: The word "all" cannot fit the שיריים, because by then some blood has already been sprinkled. So the פסוק is applied to קבלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it cannot be about the leftovers, since by then not all the blood is there, apply it to the collection.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב. The word "all" makes no sense for the leftover blood, so it must be teaching about collecting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By the time of the שיריים, part of the blood is already used up in the sprinklings. So "all the blood" can't describe that stage. This uses the rule of אם אינו ענין: a word with no job in its own context is moved to another matter, here קבלה, where "all" makes sense.

keyTerms.meaning: "If it is not needed for this matter." A word with no use in its own context is applied elsewhere.
"Apply it to the matter of..." This says where the word gets moved to.
"It is not there."

steps.confusionAlert: This answer comes from the גמרא, defending רב; it is not רב speaking. The point is that the word כׇּל, "all", can't fit the שיריים, so it is applied to קבלה.

phrases.english: If it is not needed for the matter of the leftover blood,
since not all the blood is there by then;
apply it to the matter of collecting.
phrases.notes: Some versions say בְּקַבָּלָה in round brackets; the square brackets give the corrected wording, לְקַבָּלָה. The meaning is the same.

steps.terutzResolutionType: אם אינו ענין: the word is moved from its own context to another one
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק is about שיריים only, so it can't teach about קבלה.
steps.terutzMaskana: "All" can't describe the שיריים, so the word teaches that all the blood must be collected at קבלה.
steps.whatToRemember: רב's source holds up. The word כׇּל can't apply to the leftover blood, so it teaches that all the blood must be collected.

steps.title: שמואל: The slaughterer must lift the knife up
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that the שוחט must hold the knife up, so the blood on it does not drip into the vessel. He learns this from ״וְלָקַח מִדַּם הַפָּר״: only the bull's blood, not the bull's blood mixed with something else.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: the one who slaughters must lift the knife upward, as it says, "And he shall take from the blood of the bull," and not from the blood of the bull plus something else.
steps.whatsHappening: A new rule about collecting the blood. The שוחט must keep the knife raised so the knife's blood does not mix into the vessel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The blood on the knife counts as "something else", not pure blood from the bull. שמואל reads ״מִדַּם הַפָּר״ to mean the vessel must hold only the bull's blood. So the knife must be held up, away from the vessel.

keyTerms.meaning: That he lift up.
Knife.
Something else. Here, the blood on the knife.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
The one who slaughters must lift the knife upward,
as it is said: "And he shall take from the blood of the bull"
and not from the blood of the bull and something else.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: הַשּׁוֹחֵט צָרִיךְ שֶׁיַּגְבִּיהַּ סַכִּין לְמַעְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second rule about collecting the blood. Again it is passed on by רב יהודה, but this time in the name of שמואל rather than רב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שוחט must hold the knife up so its blood does not mix into the vessel, learned from ״מִדַּם הַפָּר״ (and not something else).

steps.title: Where does he wipe off the knife's blood?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the knife's blood must not go into the vessel, what does the שוחט wipe it on?
steps.simpleTranslation: And the blood on the knife, with what does he wipe it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a practical follow-up to שמואל's rule. It is setting up אביי's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The knife still has blood on it, and that blood must be cleaned off somehow. The question is how to do that without breaking שמואל's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: With what?
Wipes off.

phrases.english: And the blood of the knife, with what does he wipe it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A practical follow-up question on שמואל's rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the שוחט wipes the knife's blood on.

steps.title: אביי: On the rim of the bowl
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the שוחט wipes the knife on the rim of the מזרק. He supports this with the bowls called ״כְּפוֹרֵי זָהָב״.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: on the rim of the bowl, as it is written, "golden bowls (כפורי)."
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question. The knife is wiped on the edge of the collecting bowl.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word כְּפוֹרֵי comes from the root כפר, which can also mean wiping. So the bowls are named for being wiped on. Wiping on the rim, and not inside the bowl, keeps the knife's blood from mixing with the bull's blood.

keyTerms.meaning: The rim of the bowl used to collect the blood.
Golden bowls. כפר can also mean "to wipe".
"As it is written."

steps.whatToRemember: The knife is held up, away from the vessel, and its blood is wiped on the rim of the מזרק. This way only the bull's own blood ends up inside the vessel.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
On the rim of the bowl,
as it is written: "golden bowls."
phrases.notes: עזרא 1:10. The word כְּפוֹרֵי can also hint at wiping, which is why אביי quotes it.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The knife is wiped on the rim of the מזרק, hinted at by ״כְּפוֹרֵי זָהָב״.

steps.title: A new rule begins: the שוחט must place something
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא quotes רב ירמיה בר אבא, who starts a new rule about what the שוחט is required to place. The sentence is cut off here and finishes in the next section.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said in the name of רב ירמיה בר אבא: The one who slaughters must place...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is opening a new statement from רב חסדא in the name of רב ירמיה בר אבא about a requirement for the שוחט. Only the first words appear here, so this line sets up a ruling that finishes in the next section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 13–15 dealt with the knife and the blood on it. Now a new אמורא adds another requirement for the שוחט, using the word צריך, meaning it is an obligation. We do not yet know what he must place or where. That detail comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who slaughters the קרבן
Must, is required to
That he place / put

keyTerms.term: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר רַב יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא
keyTerms.meaning: A chain of quotation: רב חסדא reports what רב ירמיה בר אבא said

steps.confusionAlert: Don't look for the end of the rule here. The sentence is cut off mid-thought, and what the שוחט must place is explained in the next section.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר רַב יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא:
phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda says that Rav Yirmeya bar Abba says:
One who slaughters the offering must place

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר רַב יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After אביי explained where the שוחט wipes the knife, the גמרא brings a new אמורא with another requirement for the שוחט.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שוחט is obligated to place something. The full content of the rule continues in the next section.
